title: Canon law
hookLine: the Church's law ends by saying its highest rule is the salvation of souls

lines: THE LAST PAGE OF A RULEBOOK.
THE LAST WORDS SAY WHAT IT'S FOR.
cards: Skip to the last page of a rulebook and you'll usually find an index, a clause about definitions, or nothing at all.
The Catholic Church's book of law is thick, numbered from start to finish, full of rules about marriages, parishes, property and courts.
A reader who skips to the end finds a short canon about moving a parish priest from one parish to another. And in its very last words, the whole book says what all the other rules are for.

teach.b: Canon law is the Church's own law, the rules by which the Catholic Church orders its life: who may be ordained, how a parish is set up, how a marriage case is heard.

This week has leaned on it again and again, for secular institutes, the parish, the diocese and the Holy See. The Latin Church has its Code of Canon Law; the Eastern Catholic Churches have their own code.
What canon law is not: the faith itself, or a list of everything holy.

teach.h: PLUMBING AND WIRING, NOT THE HOUSE.
teach.b: It's more like the plumbing and wiring of a house: unglamorous, mostly unnoticed, and badly missed when it fails. Now, that last canon.
It deals with a hard moment: a bishop needs to transfer a pastor who doesn't want to go.

teach.h: THE LAST CANON: THE SALVATION OF SOULS.
teach.b: The canon tells the bishop to act with fairness, what canonists call canonical equity, and to keep before his eyes the salvation of souls, which, it says, must always be the supreme law in the Church.
In Latin, the key words are salus animarum. So the book ends not with a penalty but with a purpose, and every rule in it is meant to be read in that light.
Jesus describes himself in John's Gospel, in the Douay-Rheims: "I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd giveth his life for his sheep."

teach.h: THE SUPREME LAW IN THE CHURCH.
teach.b: Canon law is the Church's attempt to organize shepherding, and its final line reminds every bishop, priest and judge that the sheep are the point.

how: Catholic dioceses have canon lawyers and church courts, called tribunals, that apply canon law, including in marriage cases. Priests and bishops study it as part of their training.

games.q: you're a bishop. a pastor refuses a transfer you believe is needed. the law gives you a procedure. what does its last line tell you to keep before your eyes?
games.why: the final canon asks for canonical equity and the salvation of souls, which must always be the supreme law in the Church.

practice: Let the last canon's idea come slowly: fairness, and before your eyes, the salvation of souls, the supreme law.

Then think of one rule you keep at home or at work, and ask what it's for, and whether it still serves the people it was made for. If you pray, bring that rule and the people it touches to God; if you don't, sit with the question.
